messages:
ravi: quick flag I think our new reranker candidate sampling for the "golden-onboard" cohort accidentally pulled some examples from the holdout set used by the offline evaluator. seeing suspiciously high NDCG on that split. anyone touched the sampling script?
anya: oh no. which split exactly? we have: train_v3, val_v2, holdout_public, holdout_private.
ravi: pipeline: `scripts/generate_cohort.py --profile golden-onboard --sample 10k` looks like it read candidate pool `pool_all_v2` instead of `pool_serving_v1` and pool_all_v2 contains holdout_private.
ci-bot: automated-eval: https://ci.redwood/evals/1781234567/golden-onboard (summary: ndcg@10 0.912, mrr 0.684)
marc: those numbers are too good for an initial bring-up. quick sanity: run a check to compute intersection with holdout_private ids. `python -c "import json; ..."` gives 423 overlaps out of 10k.
devon: 423 overlaps is non-trivial. That would inflate metrics, especially if those holdout docs are the curated goldset.
anya: is the overlap uniform or concentrated on a small set of queries? we should look at per-query recall.
olivia: pulled per-query csv. pattern: ~60% of overlapped queries have the exact gold doc included as candidate top3. also some queries have all candidates from holdout_private (ingestion bug).
ravi: command I ran to reproduce locally: `python -m cohort.diff --cohort golden-onboard --compare holdout_private_ids.csv`
marc: mitigation ideas: 1) regenerate cohort with strict pool filter (pool_serving_v1) 2) recompute eval metrics and publish corrected numbers 3) add a CI assertion that overlap_with_holdout < 1% for onboarding cohorts
devon: also add a small script to compute effective sample bias: if gold presence rate > 0.2 in candidates, mark cohort as contaminated and block promotion.
anya: timeline: I'll regenerate cohort now and kick off a fresh eval. Also opening a PR to add the overlap check to our cohort generator.
ci-bot: queued job 1781234670: regen-golden-onboard -> eval (expected ~18m)
olivia: note for postmortem: why did pool_all_v2 get into the default path? config mismatch in deploy: `COHORT_DEFAULT_POOL=pool_all_v2` set by mistake in staging envvars.
marc: thanks. add to action list: 1) revert envvar in staging 2) add integration test that validates COHORT_DEFAULT_POOL is a serving-safe pool 3) re-run any onboarding reports generated in the past 48h and mark the bad ones as superseded.
ravi: interim: what do we tell product/partners who saw the inflated numbers? I can draft a short note to be posted to the ticket tracker with corrected metrics once regen finishes.
anya: agreed. I'll attach the overlap csv and the diff so they can inspect.
devon: post-regenerate results: eval (regen) -> ndcg@10 0.862, mrr 0.631. down ~5% absolute on both vs contaminated run. I'll update ticket and mark the contaminated run as invalid.
olivia: adding follow-ups to tracker: INFR-1310 (cohort-sampling safety), INFR-1311 (cohort-ci-overlap-check), INFR-1312 (staging-envvar-audit).
marc: long-term: add deterministic hashing of candidate ids into evaluation buckets so we can quickly detect and quarantine contaminated cohorts.
ci-bot: linked issues: https://tracker.redwood/INFR-1310, https://tracker.redwood/INFR-1311
ravi: thanks team. lesson: small config flip + wide pool can silently destroy onboarding evals. will leave thread open until PRs merged. :white_check_mark:
